# Changelog — spec-tree plugin

Spec Tree methodology skills and agents: `/understand`, `/contextualize`, `/author`, `/decompose`, `/refactor`, `/align`, `/apply`, `/verify`, the audit family, and the merge lifecycle.

What changed in **this plugin**, for a consumer repository. An entry appears when a change alters what a consumer can rely on, must do, or must know.

Sections are `Breaking`, `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed`, `Requires`. `Breaking` is separate from `Changed` because a renamed skill breaks invocation outright rather than behaving differently.

A version missing below shipped without an entry. Read the gap as an absent entry, never as an absent release.

An entry is written by the changeset that ships the change. A later changeset adds one only for a release its own diff modifies or reverses, and names that release's commit — the entry is then checkable against the diff carrying it. The entry covers that commit whole, because checkability comes from naming a commit a reader can open rather than from matching lines; a commit large enough that this reaches unfamiliar content is a commit whose entry belongs to whoever shipped it. Any other backfill reconstructs what a release's consumers needed from commits and diffs alone, which produces a guess, and a guess in this file is indistinguishable from a record. A gap not reachable that way stays open.

## 0.106.3

### Changed

- **`project-run-journal` states one command form for each journal verb a streaming run uses, so an audit or review run opens, appends, seals, reads, and renders under the dangerous-command guard.** The skill gives `open`, `append`, `seal`, `read`, and `render` each as its own command with the type, run token, event path, and cursor written out literally, and stops the run at the first nonzero exit. `append` reads its event through the input redirect from a file written with the file-write tool in the session scratch directory, and the file-write tool writes only event files. The skill forbids sending an event through a heredoc, a pipe, an inline argument, or an interpreter or `printf` stage. Before this change, the skill stated the redirect form for `append` alone and described its input as read from stdin, so a consumer that built an event in the shell had the guard block its append and left an open run with no sealed verdict.

- **`/audit-implementation` records each scope-add and finding-add payload through a file, so a run records its scope one unit at a time under the dangerous-command guard.** The skill has the run driver write each payload with the file-write tool to its own file in the session scratch directory and pass the file by path to `--payload`, adds each scope unit and each finding with its own literal command, one at a time, and stops the audit with the blocked diagnostic at the first command that exits nonzero. The run-start input travels the same way: `scripts/resolve_scope.py` takes an `--output` option naming a file and writes the complete merged run-start document there, the resolved changed-path inventory and artifact selection merged with the audit input, equal to the document it prints without the option, and the skill passes that file by path to `spx verification run start --input` with no pipe and no retyped inventory. The file-write tool writes only payload files. The skill's tool grant adds the file-write tool in place of the `printf` command, and the skill no longer teaches a heredoc or a `printf` pipe for these payloads or a pipe from the resolver into the run start. Before this change, the skill taught a quoted heredoc or a `printf` pipe for every scope-add and finding-add payload and piped the resolver into the run start, so a consumer that followed it had the guard block a command in the middle of a scope sequence and left an open run with incomplete coverage. Change: https://github.com/outcomeeng/changes/issues/425.

- **`implementation-auditor` grants the file-write tool, so it can write the payload files `/audit-implementation` passes by path.** The agent that drives `/audit-implementation` now grants `Write` beside its read tools, and its constraint on edits names the payload files in the session scratch directory as the one permitted write beside the skill's `spx verification run` commands. Before this change, the agent withheld the file-write tool that the skill's payload-file form requires, which left a run open with no sealed verdict. Change: https://github.com/outcomeeng/changes/issues/425.

- **`/audit-assertions` records each scope-add and finding-add payload through a file, so a run records its scope one unit at a time under the dangerous-command guard.** The skill has the run driver write each payload with the file-write tool to its own file in the session scratch directory and pass the file by path to `--payload`, adds each scope unit and each finding with its own literal command, one at a time, and stops the audit with the blocked diagnostic at the first command that exits nonzero. The run start takes the audited spec path as its input, so it builds no payload. The file-write tool writes only payload files. The skill's tool grant adds the file-write tool in place of the `printf` command, and the skill no longer teaches a heredoc or a `printf` pipe for these payloads or states that its payloads never travel through a scratch file. Before this change, the skill taught a quoted heredoc or a `printf` pipe for every scope-add and finding-add payload, so a consumer that followed it had the guard block a command in the middle of a scope sequence and left an open run with incomplete coverage. Change: https://github.com/outcomeeng/changes/issues/425.

- **`assertion-auditor` grants the file-write tool, so it can write the payload files `/audit-assertions` passes by path.** The agent that drives `/audit-assertions` now grants `Write` in place of the `printf` command, and its constraint on edits names the payload files in the session scratch directory as the one permitted write beside the skill's `spx verification run` commands. Before this change, the agent withheld the file-write tool that the skill's payload-file form requires and granted the `printf` form the skill no longer teaches, which left a run open with no sealed verdict. Change: https://github.com/outcomeeng/changes/issues/425.

## 0.106.2

### Changed

- **`/close-change` judges a Node without a status claim from the newest Handoff and the checks of the pull request it names.** For each Node the Spec mutations blocks list, the skill runs `git cat-file -e origin/<default>:<node-path>/spx.status.json`. A Node whose directory on the default branch holds the claim is judged from `spx spec status --format json` as before. A Node whose directory holds none holds every result its merge composition selects only when the newest Handoff's `Completed blocks` line lists its block and that Handoff's `Branch or PR` line names a pull request whose every check `gh pr checks` reports for the merged head has `state` `SUCCESS`. A Handoff that names a pushed branch, an unlisted block, a failed or empty check read, and a check in any other state each refuse `Applied`. A check that concluded skipped reports `SKIPPED`, a review check skipped because the pull request modifies its own workflow file included, so a Node without a claim on such a pull request closes only once its `spx.status.json` reaches the default branch. The skill grants `gh pr checks` and `git cat-file -e`. Before this change, the skill judged every Node from `spx spec status` alone, so a Leaf whose Nodes carry no status claim could not close `Applied`.

## 0.106.0

### Breaking

- **The Change skills write, judge, and close a Change record in the final format, and a record that carries `## Nodes`, `## Assertion operations`, `## Decisions`, `## Mutations`, or `## Activities` takes the final format at its next revision.** The body opens with `## Intent`, which runs at most 60 words including its labels. Framed adds `## Governance` (each governing record with the verdict `in line`, `amended`, or `new`), `## Governance mutations` (one block per amended or new record, opening with `<path> states:`), and `## Spec mutations` (one block per Node in execution order, opening with `<path>: <malleability before> -> <malleability after>`). Sliced adds `## Slice` with `- Repository:` and `- Check:`, Executable adds no section, and a Proposed record may end with `## Open questions`. The record names no result, producer, or Verifier, because execution derives them from the merge composition. A record in another form receives no migration, alias, or inferred field: its next revision through `/author-change` authors the record anew from the proposal it carries. A Parent and its children may carry different Products. `/audit-change` counts the title's words and the Intent's words, rejects an Intent over 60 words, and judges every Governance verdict and every Spec mutations opening, and rejects an Executable record that carries execution status. `/claim-change` continues execution from the Handoff's `Next block` line, or from the first block of the record when no Handoff exists. `/release-change` writes the Handoff's `Completed blocks` and `Next block` lines in place of `Completed Mutation rows` and `Next Mutation row`. `/close-change` closes a Leaf `Applied` when the merge commit its newest Handoff names is an ancestor of the default branch, every Node its Spec mutations blocks list holds every result the merge composition selects for its malleability after, every amended or new record's Governance mutations block appears on the newest Handoff's completed-blocks line, and the Intent's Evidence is met; `/change-standards` states the same terminal rule. Before this change, these skills judged the `## Nodes`, `## Assertion operations`, `## Decisions`, and `## Mutations` record, so no final-format record passed the change audit, and a Leaf closed `Applied` only with an `## Artifacts` link for every record and Node, every link integrated, and every Node at the state its block required.

### Changed

- **`/release-change` checks the winning Claim under the `claim-record` window, names completed blocks by path with no decision-record audit token, and closes the claim window with its move to `Available`.** The winning Claim a release requires to name this session's worktree is the earliest `Claim:` after the newest Handoff that a move to `Available` follows, because an Executor posts Handoffs while the Change stays Claimed. The Handoff's `Completed blocks` line names each block by path alone, and a Governance mutations block counts as completed only when its decision-record audit approved. The Lifecycle `Available` write is the move that closes the claim window. Before this change, the skill named the winning Claim without stating its window and did not state that the line carries no audit token.
- **`/claim-change` selects the winning Claim as the earliest `Claim:` after the newest Handoff that a move to `Available` follows, and resumes from the newest Handoff's `Branch or PR` line and next block.** An Executor posts Handoffs while the Change stays Claimed, so a Handoff alone no longer ends the Claim window: the winning-Claim selection, the assignee reconciliation of a losing session, the claimed-state readback, and the failure mode and success criteria that stated the earliest Claim after the latest Handoff all apply the `claim-record` window. The claim still checks out the branch or pull request the newest Handoff names and continues execution from its `Next block` line. Before this change, the skill treated the earliest Claim after the latest Handoff as the winner, so a progress Handoff posted mid-hold made the holder's own Claim read as stale and a later losing Claim read as the winner.
- **`/close-change` treats an amended or new record as audited when the newest Handoff's completed-blocks line lists its Governance mutations block, and refuses the close naming each record whose block that line does not list.** The decision-record audit seals no verification run, so the "Decisions audited" check reads no run token and runs no `spx verification run render` command, and the skill no longer grants that command in `allowed-tools`.
- **`/execute-change` posts every Handoff with each completed block named by path and no run token, and its close reads the newest Handoff's completed-blocks line.** The decision-record audit seals no verification run, so a Governance mutations block counts as completed, and enters the `Completed blocks` line, only when its decision-record audit approves; the Handoff after each block, the Handoff after integration, and the release Handoff all list blocks by path alone, and the close reads the merge commit and the completed-blocks line from the newest Handoff. The skill states that a PDR or ADR audit returns its verdict without a sealed run. Before this change, the Executor followed each completed Governance mutations block with the run token of its approving decision-record audit and expected the close to read that token.
- **`/change-standards` states that a Handoff carries no decision-record audit run token, and a close treats a record as audited when the newest Handoff lists its block as completed.** The decision-record audit seals no verification run, so the `handoff-record` rule's `Completed blocks` line names each completed block by path with no token, and a Governance mutations block counts as completed only when its decision-record audit approved. The Handoff the Executor posts after integration names every block as completed, and the rule admits `none` on its `Next block` line there. The terminal rule for `Applied` requires each amended or new record to be audited, which the newest Handoff's `Completed blocks` line lists. Before this change, the line followed each completed Governance mutations block with the run token of its approving decision-record audit, and a close read that token from the newest Handoff.
- **`/change-standards` admits a Handoff the Executor posts after every completed block and after integration without releasing the Change, and a close reads the merge commit and the completed blocks from the newest Handoff.** The `handoff-record` rule states that the `Branch or PR` line carries the full head commit, and the merged pull request with its merge commit after integration; the `Completed blocks` line names each completed block by path. A Handoff posted without a release leaves the Claim in force, and the winning Claim is the earliest `Claim:` after the newest Handoff that a move to `Available` follows. The no-execution-status rule names the same Handoff content. Before this change, only a release posted a Handoff, the line named the stopping commit alone, and a close found no completed blocks in any Handoff.
- **`/change-standards` states that the Handoff's `Branch or PR` line carries the head commit with the branch or pull request.** The `handoff-record` rule fixes the line as the pushed work branch or the PR URL followed by `@` and the full head commit SHA, or `none`, and states that a reader takes the changeset from the branch or pull request and the commit as the state the Handoff describes; the no-execution-status rule names the same content. Before this change, the line carried the branch or PR URL alone, so a Handoff did not name the commit its work stopped at.
- **`/release-change` writes the head commit on the Handoff's `Branch or PR` line.** The line names the pushed work branch or the open PR URL, followed by `@` and the full head commit SHA that `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` prints after the push check, and stays `none` for a checkout without local work; the result returns the branch or PR with that commit. Before this change, the line carried the branch name or PR URL alone, so a Handoff did not name the commit its work stopped at.
- **`/change-standards` states the final-format Change record once, and each Maturity's Definition of Ready judges a record against those rules by identifier.** The `<record_rules>` fix the front matter keys, the section set and order, the 15-word title and 60-word Intent limits, the Leaf, Parent, and root types derived from the mutations blocks and `parent`, and the rules for `## Governance`, `## Governance mutations`, `## Spec mutations`, `## Slice`, `## Open questions`, and `## Artifacts`. The `product` key names the one Product that owns the Change's Output, and a Parent and its children may carry different Products. A Definition of Ready criterion cites the record rule it applies and adds only its own level's condition; the Executable Definition of Ready also carries the `<merge_composition>` that execution applies and judges that the record carries no execution status: no `## Artifacts` section, no Node state, and no progress, which a Handoff alone records. A Spec mutations block opening carries no required state, a Leaf's `Applied` follows from the merge commit its newest Handoff names being an ancestor of the default branch, every Node holding every result its merge composition selects, and every amended or new record's Governance mutations block listed on the newest Handoff's completed-blocks line, and a record that carries `## Artifacts` is outside the final format. The lifecycle reference states the Handoff's `Completed blocks` and `Next block` lines. A record in the `# Output` form, or any other form outside the contract, receives no judgment, migration, alias, or inferred field. Before this change, the standards judged the `## Nodes`, `## Assertion operations`, `## Decisions`, and `## Mutations` record, and each Definition of Ready restated those rules; the Executable record carried `## Artifacts` links and each Spec mutations opening's required state, and a Leaf closed `Applied` against them.
- **`/understand` states the final Change record's coordination model.** The foundation states that a Change carries its Product and Intent, lists the Lifecycle values `Submitted`, `Available`, `Claimed`, `Applied`, and `Abandoned`, and types a Leaf by its `## Governance mutations` and `## Spec mutations` blocks, which a Parent hands to its children. The record carries no execution status, so execution records its progress only in the Handoff, which names the completed blocks and the next block. Execution begins only on a Claimed, Executable Leaf whose every predecessor is closed and whose blockers are resolved. The Executor takes the mutation blocks in order, and the Refiner is the operator's conversation without a statement of how it is realized. Before this change, it described a received input and a reason for the work, a Leaf's `## Mutations` rows, an Executor that took Mutation rows, a Handoff of completed Mutation rows, and `## Artifacts` links to produced content, which the Change skills no longer read.
- **`/author-change` authors every Maturity's record in the final format, and an Executable record carries no execution status.** The four templates open with `## Intent` under the 60-word limit; the Proposed template ends with an optional `## Open questions`, and the Framed, Sliced, and Executable templates carry `## Governance`, `## Governance mutations`, and `## Spec mutations` in place of `## Nodes`, `## Assertion operations`, `## Decisions`, and `## Mutations`, with the Sliced and Executable templates adding `## Slice`. The Executable template has the Sliced template's sections, and the Executable workflow writes no result, producer, or Verifier and no execution status into the record: no Node state, no `## Artifacts` link to produced content, and no progress, which execution records only in its Handoff. The Sliced workflow splits a source into children that carry their share of the Intent, mutations blocks, and settled decisions, with each child's `product` naming the Product that owns its Output, and writes `## Slice` for a Leaf. A record published in another form takes the final format at its next revision, authored anew from the proposal it carries. A record that carries `## Artifacts` also takes the final format at its next revision. Before this change, the skill authored the `## Nodes`, `## Assertion operations`, `## Decisions`, and `## Mutations` record, and an Executable record carried `## Artifacts` links and each Spec mutations opening's required state, which the Change audit and execution no longer accept.
- **`/execute-change` derives each block's results and Verifiers from the merge composition and reads none from the record.** The Executor takes the `## Governance mutations` blocks, then the `## Spec mutations` blocks, each in record order, and selects the producing definition from the content a block produces and the Verifiers from the `merge_composition` of `/change-standards` for the Node's malleability after and the tags of its assertions: the decision-record audit for a Governance block, and the evidence audits and the `[audit]` assertion audit a Spec block's malleability and tags select. It types a Leaf by those blocks, so a record that carries neither block is refused as a Parent or root, continues from the Handoff's `Next block` line or the first block of the record, writes no `## Artifacts` link and no other progress into the record, and states the `Completed blocks` and `Next block` lines of the Handoff it releases from the newest earlier Handoff and the blocks its session completed. The spec, implementation, and Change-record auditor rows leave the Verifier table, because the composition selects none of them for a block. Before this change, the skill selected definitions and Verifiers from the results a `## Mutations` row named, typed a Leaf from `## Nodes`, and recorded each completed block as an `## Artifacts` link and pinned the links to the merge commit, so it could not execute a record in the final format.
- **`/audit-change` measures the title's words and the `## Intent` section's words and no longer counts sentences or `## Decisions` rows, and it compares no Parent's Product with its children's.** The runner's `count-limits` operation returns the title entry, with a limit of 15 words, and one `Intent` entry, with a limit of 60 words counting its labels, and its `violations` list carries each entry over its limit; the per-part sentence entries, the `Decisions rows` entry, and the per-answer entries leave the result. The `change-type` judgment finds a defect when a record carries a Governance mutations or Spec mutations block while the store lists children, or is Executable while it lists children, and finds none from a Product that differs between a Parent and a child. A Spec mutations block opening carries no required state, and the skill judges an Executable record against `executable-no-status`, so a `## Artifacts` section, a link to produced content, a Node's state, or a record of progress is a defect. The skill's description names the final format. Before this change, the operation counted sentences in each Intent part and in each Decisions answer, the judgment rejected a record whose Product differed from a child's or from its Parent's, and an Executable record was judged for the required state each Spec mutations opening carried.
- **`/claim-change` names the first block of the record, not the first block with no Artifacts link, as the point execution starts from when no Handoff exists.** The result still names the newest Handoff's `Branch or PR` line and continues from its `Next block` line. A final-format record carries no `## Artifacts` link, so the first `## Governance mutations` block, or the first `## Spec mutations` block when the record has none, is the start. Before this change, the skill looked for a block with no `## Artifacts` link, which a final-format record never carries.
- **`/release-change` derives the Handoff's `Completed blocks` from the newest earlier Handoff and this session's pushed work, not from `## Artifacts` links.** A block counts as completed when the newest earlier Handoff lists it or this session's pushed work produced its results, and the skill reads no progress from the record. The refinement step no longer names Artifacts links as record content. Before this change, a block counted as completed when `## Artifacts` linked its record or Node, which a final-format record never carries, so a Handoff could never list a completed block.
- **`/claim-change` reads the branch or pull request from the text before `@` on the Handoff's `Branch or PR` line.** The line holds the pushed work branch or the PR URL, then `@` and the full head commit SHA, or `none`; the checkout step takes the text before `@` as the branch to fetch and switch to, or the pull request whose head branch it resolves, and the result still returns the whole line. Before this change, the skill treated the whole line as the branch or pull request, so a line carrying the head commit named no fetchable branch.
- **`/execute-change` posts a Handoff after every completed block and after `/merge` reports the changeset merged, while the Change stays Claimed, and its close reads the newest one.** After the Verifiers approve a block's head, the Executor pushes the work branch and posts a Handoff in the `handoff-record` shape: the `Branch or PR` line carries the pushed branch with the full head commit, and the `Completed blocks` line names each completed block by path. After the merge, the Handoff names the merged pull request with its merge commit and `none` as the next block, and a restarted Executor whose newest Handoff is that one goes straight to the close, which reads the merge commit and the completed blocks from it. The record receives no write. Before this change, the Executor wrote a Handoff only when it released the Change, so a close found no merge commit and no completed blocks for a Change it had integrated.
- **`/execute-change` reads the branch or pull request from the text before `@` on the Handoff's `Branch or PR` line.** The line holds the pushed work branch or the PR URL, then `@` and the full head commit SHA, or `none`; the step that brings the work into the worktree takes the text before `@` as the branch to fetch and switch to, or the pull request whose head branch it resolves, and `none` still starts a new branch. Before this change, the skill treated the whole line as the branch or pull request, so a line carrying the head commit named no fetchable branch.
- **`/close-change` types a Change by its mutations blocks and closes a Leaf `Applied` against the merge commit its newest Handoff names and the results held from current state.** The skill derives Leaf, Parent, or root from the body's mutations blocks and the store's `Parent` values. For a Leaf, the Integrated check reads the newest Handoff's `Branch or PR` line, takes the pull request's merge commit or the pushed branch's tip on origin, and requires it to be an ancestor of the default branch, refusing the close when no Handoff, a Handoff naming `none`, or a pull request with no merge commit leaves nothing to check. The Results held check requires `spx spec status --format json` to report each Node of the `## Spec mutations` blocks holding every result the merge composition selects for its malleability after, and the Decisions audited check requires the newest Handoff's completed-blocks line to list each amended or new record's `## Governance mutations` block; each refuses the close naming what is short. The skill reads no `## Artifacts` link and no required state from a block opening. Before this change, the skill typed a Change from `## Nodes` and `## Mutations`, required an Artifacts link for every record and Node and a pinned merge commit on each link, and checked each Node against the state its block required.

- **`/close-change` loads the merge composition and selects the winning Claim under the `claim-record` window.** The skill loads `/change-standards` with `Executable`, as `/execute-change` does, so the Results held check judges each Node of the `## Spec mutations` blocks against the results the `merge_composition` selects for its malleability after and the tags of its assertions. The skill selects the winning Claim as the earliest `Claim:` after the newest Handoff that a move to `Available` follows, and reads the newest Handoff whether a release or an Executor progress Handoff posted it. Before this change, the skill never loaded the composition, so the Results held check could not be decided from the skill's own inputs.

- **`/close-change` reads the branch or pull request from the text before `@` on the Handoff's `Branch or PR` line.** The line holds the pushed work branch or the PR URL, then `@` and the full head commit SHA, or `none`; the Integrated check takes the text before `@` as the pull request whose merge commit it reads or the pushed branch whose tip on origin it reads, and still requires that commit to be an ancestor of the default branch, never the recorded SHA. Before this change, the skill treated the whole line as the branch or pull request, so a line carrying the head commit named no pull request or branch to resolve.

- **The Change record's front-matter key for absorbed Changes is `predecessors`, and `/audit-change`, `/author-change`, `/change-standards`, and `/understand` read and write that key.** The closed key set is `title`, `product`, `maturity`, `lifecycle`, `predecessors`, `blocked_by`, and `parent`, and the outside-contract test compares a record's front matter with it, so a record that carries `refined_from` is outside the contract and one that carries `predecessors` is admitted. The four `/author-change` templates carry `predecessors: []`, a merge closes the absorbed Change `Abandoned` and adds it to the survivor's `predecessors`, and persistence writes `predecessors` to the `Predecessors` issue field and reads it back unchanged. Before this change, the key was `refined_from`, which a stored record that follows this change must rename at its next revision.

## 0.105.6

### Fixed

- **`/execute-change` starts on its worktree's branch when neither the record nor the newest Handoff names a working branch, instead of releasing before any round.** The Executor works on the branch its assigned worktree has checked out only when that branch is not the default branch and its name ends with the Change number, as `work/change-<N>` and `executor-<N>` do, so a stale branch an interrupted release left in the worktree is never adopted for an unrelated Change. Otherwise the worktree counts as naming no branch, and the Executor creates `work/change-<N>` from the Change's number, on a detached checkout, the default branch, or a branch whose name does not end with the number. A branch the record or the newest Handoff names stays the working branch, and the Handoff's wins over the record's. Before this change, a first start on a record that named no branch went to the release step with that gap as the blocker, so Executors for such Changes released without running a round.

## 0.105.5

### Changed

- **`/test` loads the test skill of each language in which it creates or changes a test file before its first write, in a repair round as in a new scaffold.** The load is its own step ahead of scaffolding, once per language: an existing file's language follows from its canonical filename rendering and a new file's from the node's implementation and existing tests. A language with no installed test skill is reported with the result, and a decision-rule invocation loads none. Before this change, `/test` loaded a language test skill only while scaffolding a new test, so a round that repaired an existing test wrote without that language's test skill or its standards. The `change-tester` definition is unchanged and every caller of `/test` receives the same load. The conditional four-part progression detail moves from the `/test` body into a bundled reference that the body cites, which keeps the body under its line ceiling.

## 0.105.4

### Fixed

- **`/audit-assertions` records one root unit for the audited node spec and each `[audit]` assertion as that root's child, so a run on a spec with several `[audit]` assertions seals.** The root's `unitId` is the audited spec path, it carries no `parentUnitId`, and each child keeps its unit key `assertion:<designator>:<path>` and names the root as its parent. Class `spec`, kind `spec`, and the spec path as subject apply to the root and to every child. A spec with no `[audit]` assertion records no unit and finishes `approved`, because the root exists to contain assertion units. Before this change, the skill recorded every assertion as a root, and `spx` admits one root per file-scoped run, so the second unit was refused and no run on a spec with several `[audit]` assertions finished.

## 0.105.3

### Fixed

- **`/audit-assertions` records each scope unit with audit class `spec` and audit kind `spec`, so a run it starts can finish.** The unit's subject stays the audited node spec path, and the assertion's designator, its rule slug or `ordinal-<n>` when pathless, sits in the unit key and opens the message of every finding on that unit. A finding on that unit carries `producerProvenance` with the plugin version, which the skill reads through `spec-tree:spec-tree-plugin`. A consumer reads an `[audit]` assertion's result from the sealed run, which the pinned `spx` accepts for this payload. Before this change, the skill recorded audit class `assertion`, which `spx` refuses, so a run could not record its first unit, and its finding payload lacked `producerProvenance`, which `spx` rejects, so no run with a finding could seal; no `[audit]` result came from a sealed run.

## 0.105.2

### Changed

- **The merge policy of `merging-standards` dispatches the evidence audits for each touched `implementation`-malleable node whose evidence result is missing or invalidated, and a change to reached implementation alone invalidates it.** A node's evidence pin names its spec, its `tests/` or `evals/` directory, and the implementation files its linked verification reaches. Any difference in a pinned path invalidates the result, unless the toolchain proves deterministically that every changed pinned path is a spec and every change in those specs is a link-format edit; an unproven exception leaves the result invalidated, and a node with no status claim or no passed evidence entry has a missing result and takes the audit. A `spec`- or `verification`-malleable node takes no evidence audit. After a clean rebase, a converged evidence-auditor verdict is reused only when the branch patch is unchanged and, in addition, no base-delta path is one that node's pin reads or the same proof holds for each such path. Before this change, an evidence Auditor was dispatched only where the diff created or modified `[test]` or `[eval]` assertions, linked evidence files, or the test infrastructure they import, so a changeset that changed only reached production code took no evidence audit at merge, and a verdict was reused across a rebase unless the base delta touched a governed evidence surface.
- **The Executable merge composition of `change-standards` names the nodes the evidence audits cover.** The composition in `dor-executable.md` now selects the evidence audits for each touched `implementation`-malleable node whose evidence result is missing or invalidated, including by a change to reached implementation alone, and for no `spec`- or `verification`-malleable node, matching the merge policy. A Change's `## Mutations` rows name those audits for exactly those nodes. Before this change, the composition read "adds the evidence audits and Review" without naming the nodes.

## 0.105.1

### Changed

- **`change-standards` states that `## Artifacts` links the audited content each round has produced and is empty before the first round, so an Executable record passes its change audit before its first round.** The `artifacts` rule and the `executable-artifacts` criterion judge each link present: a link must name a Node in `## Nodes` and pin the commit that holds its audited content, and an empty section satisfies the criterion. The completeness check moves to the close, where the `terminal-record` rule of the Lifecycle reference requires `Applied` for a Leaf to carry a link for every Node the Change adds, modifies, or implements. Before this change, the rule and the criterion required a link for every such Node, which no Executable record revised before execution could hold, and the audit rejected an empty section.
- **`/close-change` refuses `Applied` for a Leaf while a Node the Change adds, modifies, or implements has no `## Artifacts` link.** The Leaf precondition gains the check beside the integration, Required-state, and Intent checks, and the refusal names the Node without a link. Before this change, the close checked only that each link present was integrated, so a Leaf with a Node lacking a link could close `Applied`.

## 0.105.0

### Added

- **`/audit-assertions` judges each `[audit]` assertion of one node spec against the subject the assertion names.** The skill takes the spec path and a run-driver identity, starts one file-scoped `spx verification run` before judging with the audited path as its input, so the retained input equals the audited file, records one scope unit per `[audit:{rule-slug}]` assertion keyed by its slug (a pathless `[audit]` assertion by its ordinal in the spec) with every finding on its unit, seals the run, and returns the run token with the rendered projection, or the complete `BLOCKED` diagnostic when a command fails. The run rejects only on a finding on touched text, the text the changeset adds, changes, or invalidates, measured against the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/HEAD` in the live working tree; each other finding follows the projection as a `filed` line with its key, its `baseRefEvidence`, and its `issuesEntry`, so a standing defect in an audited subject never blocks an unrelated merge. It judges no assertion carrying another tag and never judges how an assertion is declared or selected, which stays with `/audit-specs`. It grants no file-write tool, so it passes each payload to `spx verification run` on stdin in the quoted-heredoc or one-line `printf` form `/audit-implementation` uses, as the `audit_skill_grants` rule requires of an `audit-*` skill, and its `Bash(printf '%s\n':*)` grant matches the agent's. It keys each recorded finding `<unitId>:<rule>`, so the same finding carries the same key in every run and in the `filed` line. A consumer reads an `[audit]` assertion's result from the sealed run, where before this change no skill produced one.
- **`assertion-auditor` is the isolated agent that runs `/audit-assertions`.** It holds read-only observation tools, `Bash(spx verification run:*)`, `Bash(printf '%s\n':*)` for the one-line stdin form, and `Bash(git merge-base:*)` and `Bash(git diff:*)` for the touched-text classification against the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/HEAD`, and no file-write tool. It takes a node spec path, supplies its own run-driver identity, and returns the run token with the rendered projection, or the complete `BLOCKED` diagnostic, unchanged. A caller dispatches it to obtain the verdict on a node's `[audit]` assertions from a separate session and reads that verdict from the sealed run.

### Changed

- **`/execute-change` launches `assertion-auditor` as the Verifier for an evidence obligation on a node's `[audit]` assertions and reads its verdict from the sealed run whose token the launch returns.** The Verifier table gains the row for a node's `[audit]` assertions, and the terminal-status rule that governed the skill and subagent auditors now covers this launch: `approved` approves, and `rejected` rejects whatever the finding count. A Frame that requires an `[audit]` result now names a Verifier the Executor can launch. Before this change, the table named no Verifier for `[audit]` assertions, and an Executor whose Frame required one stopped.

## 0.104.9

### Breaking

- **`change-standards` states a seven-key Change record, and a record with the six-key front matter is outside the contract.** The closed key set gains `parent`, the canonical identity of the Parent Change or `null`. `lifecycle` takes `Available`, `Claimed`, `Submitted`, `Applied`, or `Abandoned`: no skill writes or accepts `Refined`, and `refined_from` lists the Changes this Change absorbed by a merge rather than its predecessors. Sliced records carry `## Mutations` and Executable records add `## Artifacts` in place of `## Slice` and `## Activities`; a record that carries the old sections takes the new ones at its next revision. Before this change, the standards required the six keys, admitted `Refined`, and required `## Slice` and `## Activities`.

### Changed

- **`change-standards` types each Change as a Leaf, a Parent, or a root and bounds the record's length.** A Change that names Nodes is a Leaf, a Change that another Change names in `parent` is a Parent that carries neither `## Nodes` nor `## Assertion operations` and never reaches Executable, and a Change with neither is a root, which may carry no Product. `## Nodes` states each Node's Malleability before and after the Change. The title has at most 15 words, each Intent part one to three sentences, `## Decisions` at most 12 rows, and each answer at most two sentences. The Lifecycle reference reads children from the `Parent` issue field, reads the Change that absorbed a given Change as the store record whose `Predecessors` value names it, through the same bounded issues page (100 issues per page, at most 10 pages), names the completed Mutation rows and the next one in the Handoff, and closes a Leaf `Applied` only once its Artifacts links are integrated, its Nodes are at their required states, and the Intent's Evidence is met, and a Parent only once its last child closed `Applied`.
- **`/author-change` writes each record from its Maturity's own template and splits, merges, and reframes a Change without writing `Refined`.** The skill ships `proposed.md`, `framed.md`, `sliced.md`, and `executable.md` templates in place of one `change.md`; none carries `## Slice` or `## Activities`. Every record carries the seven keys, including `parent`, with the title, each Intent part, and `## Decisions` within the record limits. Framed records state each Node's Malleability before and after, Sliced Leaves write `## Mutations` with the one repository, the one observable check, and one row per Node in execution order, and Executable Leaves name in each row the results and producers the merge composition selects and add `## Artifacts`, which `/execute-change` fills after each round. A split creates children that name the source in `parent` and drops the source's `## Nodes` and `## Assertion operations`; a merge closes the absorbed Change `Abandoned` and appends it to the survivor's `refined_from`; a reframe lowers the Change to `Proposed` in place. A Parent never reaches Executable. Persistence reads back the `Parent` issue field beside `Predecessors`, and a new decision that has not merged is posted as a comment on the Change's issue that `## Artifacts` links. Before this change, the skill wrote six keys, `## Slice` and `## Activities`, and closed the source of a split or coalescence `Refined`.
- **`/audit-change` counts the record's length limits and rejects the Parent defects, against the seven-key record.** The key-set check and the `OUTSIDE_CONTRACT` result list `parent` beside the six earlier keys, so a six-key record is outside the contract. The runner's new `count-limits` operation returns the title's words, each Intent part's sentences, the `## Decisions` rows, and each answer's sentences with their limits, and the audit records one `record-limits` finding for each count over its limit, naming the section, the limit, and the count. The runner's new `read-relations` operation reads the store's `Product` and `Parent` values, and the audit rejects a record that carries `## Nodes` or `## Assertion operations` while another Change names it in `parent`, a Parent at Executable, a Parent whose Product differs from the Product of any of its children, and a child whose Product differs from its Parent's. Before this change, the audit counted no section's length, expected six keys, and judged no Parent structure.
- **`/claim-change` claims a root that carries no Product and continues from the Handoff's Next Mutation row.** The precondition, the candidate listing, and the readback accept a Product that equals the configured Product or is empty for a root, and read back a root's Product still empty. Execution at Executable resumes from the Handoff's Next Mutation row or the first uncompleted `## Mutations` row. Before this change, the skill claimed only a Change whose Product equalled the configured Product and resumed from the Handoff's Next Activity or the first unchecked Activity.
- **`/release-change` writes the Handoff's Mutation rows and releases a root that carries no Product.** The Handoff names `Completed Mutation rows` and `Next Mutation row` from the body's `## Mutations` rows by Node path, with `none` for a Parent, and keeps `refinement: <Maturity> → <next level>` and `confirmation: <Maturity>` as the Next Mutation row below Executable and for `submit`. The body revision before the release folds in completed Mutation rows and Artifacts links. The readback requires Product unchanged, the overlay Product or empty for a root. Before this change, the Handoff read `Completed Activities` and `Next Activity` from the `## Activities` checklist, and the readback required Product to equal the overlay Product.
- **`/close-change` refuses `Refined`, closes by the Change's type, and closes Parents upward.** The argument takes `Applied` or `Abandoned`. A Leaf closes `Applied` once every `## Artifacts` link pins a merge commit that `git merge-base --is-ancestor` finds on the default branch, every Node in `## Nodes` is at the Required state its row names, and the Intent's Evidence is met. A Parent closes `Applied` only when every child is closed and the last to close closed `Applied`, and stays open when a child is open or the last closed `Abandoned`. A root closes only on the operator's direction, and the readback accepts an empty Product for it. After a Leaf or Parent closes `Applied` and its Parent has a Parent and no open child, the same session claims that Parent through `/claim-change` and closes it `Applied`, repeating upward and never closing a root. Before this change, the skill accepted `Refined` with at least one successor in the store and required every Activity checked for `Applied`.
- **`/execute-change` executes an Executable Leaf through its `## Mutations` rows and records `## Artifacts` links.** The skill takes the rows in record order and selects each round's definition from the row's transition and the results it names for its Node; an add or modify selects `change-author`, an implement selects the Node's implementation definition, and a skill-surface row's transition selects the `create-skill` intent. After each row's Verifiers approve, `/author-change` records the audited content as an `## Artifacts` link, and after `/merge` it pins every link to the merge commit that `/close-change` requires. It refuses a Parent and a root that names no Nodes, requires every predecessor closed and every blocker resolved in place of `Refined` predecessors, resolving a blocker closed `Abandoned` through the absorber lookup, and resumes from the Handoff's Next Mutation row. Before this change, the skill ran a Change's Activities in order, required every predecessor `Refined`, and checked Activities off in the record.
- **The `/understand` foundation states the Leaf, Parent, and root Change model.** The coordination model names the Lifecycle values `Available`, `Claimed`, `Submitted`, `Applied`, and `Abandoned`; the Leaf, Parent, and root types; a Leaf's `## Mutations` and `## Artifacts`; a Handoff naming the completed Mutation rows and the next one; and execution only on a Claimed, Executable Leaf whose every predecessor is closed and whose blockers are resolved. The projection paragraph keeps the claim's writer and the merge outcomes, and the gate composition by malleability moves to `references/status-claims.md`, which holds the rendered `SKILL.md` under 40,000 code points in both runtimes. Before this change, the foundation named `Refined` Status, lineage leaves with `Refined` predecessors, and Activities.
- **The `change-author` description names the launch as a Mutation row that needs spec-tree artifacts.** `/execute-change` launches the round by exact name when a `## Mutations` row adds or modifies a decision, spec, node, or note that `/author` writes. Before this change, the description named the launch as an Activity that needs those artifacts.
- **The `change-verifier` description names the launch as a Mutation row that needs routed assertions and evidence.** `/execute-change` launches the round by exact name when a Mutation row needs assertions routed to their verification type and evidence produced or repaired through `/verify`. Before this change, the description named the launch as an Activity that needs them.
- **The `change-tester` description names the launch as a Mutation row that needs routed `[test]` evidence.** `/execute-change` launches the round by exact name when a Mutation row needs routed `[test]` evidence produced or repaired through `/test`. Before this change, the description named the launch as an Activity that needs that evidence.
- **The `change-implementer` description names the launch as a Mutation row that needs a language implementation.** `/execute-change` launches the round by exact name when a Mutation row needs a language implementation of one node produced or repaired through `/implement-change`. Before this change, the description named the launch as an Activity that needs a language implementation.
- **The `change-skill-author` description names the launch as a Mutation row that needs a skill surface.** `/execute-change` launches the round by exact name when a Mutation row needs a skill surface (a `SKILL.md`, another file in a skill directory, or an authored shared fragment) produced or repaired through `instructions:create-skill`. Before this change, the description named the launch as an Activity that needs a skill surface.
- **The `change-subagent-author` description names the launch as a Mutation row that needs a subagent definition.** `/execute-change` launches the round by exact name when a Mutation row needs a subagent definition produced or repaired through `instructions:create-subagent`. Before this change, the description named the launch as an Activity that needs a subagent definition.
- **The managed instruction-block template routes a terminal Change to `/close-change <Applied|Abandoned>` and takes version 0.42.0.** The Change Lifecycle section names no `Refined` value, so every consumer's root routers read stale at 0.41.0 and regenerate through `/update-instruction-block`. Before this change, the section routed a terminal Change to `/close-change <Applied|Refined|Abandoned>` at template version 0.41.0.

Before this change, the skill taught both stdin forms, which the dangerous-command guard refuses when a message carries code spans or shell text.

The agent never removes a payload file. The dangerous-command guard section no longer exempts a payload pipe: every pipe between two operations is a composition the parts cannot carry, and an input redirect from a payload scratch file holds one operation. Before this change, the skill taught reading the event from stdin, which the dangerous-command guard refuses when an event carries code spans, quotes, or JSON.

## 0.104.7

### Changed

- **`/audit-implementation` rejects a changeset only for a finding on touched text and returns every other finding as `filed`.** Touched text is a line the `base..head` scope adds or changes, extended to its enclosing sentence, assertion, rule, or declaration, plus the text the change invalidates: text that cites, quotes, restates, or depends on changed text and now disagrees with it, a rule a changed line newly violates in another file, and generated output whose source changed. The run records only a finding on touched text, so the sealed projection's `terminalStatus` is `approved` when no such finding exists, whatever standing findings the concerns report. After the projection, the response lists each other finding on a `filed:` line carrying its key, rule identifier, run token, and its `baseRefEvidence` diff range showing every location lies outside the change, and its `issuesEntry` naming the governing node's `ISSUES.md` path and entry heading, or `filed: none`. A finding's severity never decides the verdict, and a finding keeps the severity and disposition recorded for its key across runs: its severity rises, or a `filed` finding starts to reject, only when the run names a changed basis in the finding's evidence. Before this change, any recorded finding rejected the run, wherever it lay.
- **`/audit-specs` rejects a node spec only for a finding on touched text and returns every other finding with severity `FILED`.** Touched text is a line of the spec that differs between the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/HEAD` and the live file, extended to its enclosing sentence or assertion, plus the text the change invalidates; a spec absent at the base is touched in full. The verdict is `APPROVED` when no `REJECT` finding exists, whatever `FILED` findings it carries. Each `FILED` finding adds `key` (`<node-spec-file-path>:<location>:<rule>`), `baseRefEvidence` (the diff range showing every location lies outside the change), and `issuesEntry` (the `path` and entry `heading` in the governing node's `ISSUES.md`) to the usual finding fields and fails no row. A finding keeps the severity recorded for its key in the node's `ISSUES.md` across runs, and rises or starts to reject only when the run names a changed basis in its evidence. Before this change, any finding in the spec rejected it, wherever it lay.
- **`/audit-tests` rejects a spec node's tests only for a finding on touched text and returns every other finding with severity `FILED`.** Touched text is a line of an inventoried artifact (the spec's assertions, each linked test, and every harness, generator, fixture, discovery artifact, and governed production source of the evidence chain) that differs between the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/HEAD` and the live file, extended to its enclosing assertion, test function, or declaration, plus the text the change invalidates; an artifact absent at the base is touched in full. The verdict is `APPROVED` when no `REJECT` finding exists, whatever `FILED` findings it carries, and a finding folded in from a language test audit takes the same classification. Each `FILED` finding adds `key` (`<file>:<assertion-or-declaration>:<property>:<rule>`), `baseRefEvidence` (the diff range showing every location lies outside the change), and `issuesEntry` (the `path` and entry `heading` in the governing node's `ISSUES.md`) to the nine canonical fields and fails no row. A finding keeps the severity recorded for its key in the node's `ISSUES.md` across runs, and rises or starts to reject only when the run names a changed basis. Before this change, any finding in the evidence rejected it, wherever it lay.
- **`/audit-eval-evidence` rejects a spec node's eval suite only for a finding on touched text and returns every other finding with severity `FILED`.** Touched text is a line of an inspected artifact (the spec's `[eval]` assertions, `eval.toml`, the prompt, the cases, `history.jsonl`, the prompt template, and the producer artifact or selected producer section) that differs between the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/HEAD` and the live file, extended to its enclosing assertion, table, case record, history row, or section, plus the text the change invalidates; an artifact absent at the base is touched in full. The verdict is `FAIL` only when a `REJECT` finding exists, whatever `FILED` findings it carries. Each `FILED` finding adds `key` (`<file>:<assertion>:<rule>`), `baseRefEvidence` (the diff range showing every location lies outside the change), and `issuesEntry` (the `path` and entry `heading` in the governing node's `ISSUES.md`) to the usual finding fields and fails no row. A finding keeps the severity recorded for its key in the node's `ISSUES.md` across runs, and rises or starts to reject only when the run names a changed basis. Before this change, any failed evidence property in the suite rejected it, wherever it lay.
- **`/audit-adr` rejects an ADR only for a finding on touched text and returns every other finding with severity `filed`.** Touched text is a line of the ADR that differs between the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/HEAD` and the live file, extended to its enclosing sentence, rule, or decision statement, plus the text the change invalidates; an ADR absent at the base is touched in full. The verdict is `APPROVED` when no `blocking` finding exists, whatever `filed` findings it carries, and a finding folded in from a language architecture audit takes the same classification. Each `filed` finding adds `key` (`<adr-file-path>:<location>:<rule>`), `baseRefEvidence` (the diff range showing every location lies outside the change), and `issuesEntry` (the `path` and entry `heading` in the governing node's `ISSUES.md`) to the usual finding fields and fails no row. A finding keeps the severity recorded for its key in the node's `ISSUES.md` across runs, and rises or starts to reject only when the run names a changed basis. Before this change, any finding in the ADR rejected it, wherever it lay.
- **`/audit-pdr` rejects a PDR only for a finding on touched text and returns every other finding with severity `FILED`.** Touched text is a line of the PDR that differs between the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/HEAD` and the live file, extended to its enclosing sentence, property, rule, or decision statement, plus the text the change invalidates; a PDR absent at the base is touched in full. The verdict is `APPROVED` when no `REJECT` finding exists, whatever `FILED` findings it carries. Each `FILED` finding adds `key` (`<pdr-file-path>:<location>:<rule>`), `baseRefEvidence` (the diff range showing every location lies outside the change), and `issuesEntry` (the `path` and entry `heading` in the governing node's `ISSUES.md`) to the usual finding fields and fails no row. A finding keeps the severity recorded for its key in the node's `ISSUES.md` across runs, and rises or starts to reject only when the run names a changed basis. `/audit-pdr` also grants `git merge-base` and `git diff` in its `allowed-tools` for the touched-text resolution and names its `spec-tree:understand`, `spec-tree:contextualize`, and `spec-tree:test-evidence-standards` dependencies in the composed `Use skill` form. Before this change, any finding in the PDR rejected it, wherever it lay.
- **`/audit-change` rejects a Change record only for a finding on touched text and returns every other finding as `filed`.** A new record, or a request with no published body, is touched in full. A revision touches its front matter, each `##` section that differs from the published body, and the unchanged text those changes make false. A finding on any other section takes severity `filed`, fails no run, and is listed after the `finish` result on a `filed:` line carrying its idempotency key, rule, run token, and the section that equals the published body, or `filed: none`. A `filed` finding carries a top-level `baseRefEvidence` string, the issue identity and the headings of the sections that equal the published body, and a top-level `issuesEntry` object with the strings `path` and `heading` that locate the entry recording it in an `ISSUES.md`; the installed `spx` rejects a `filed` finding without them, and a `blocking` finding carries neither. A `filed` finding rises to `blocking` only when its evidence names a changed basis. The run finishes `approved` when no `blocking` finding exists. Before this change, a finding on an untouched section of a revision took severity `debt` and the run finished `rejected`.
- **`/author-change` sweeps every same-class site and every section a repair changes before it dispatches a second change audit, and treats a `filed` finding as outside the rejection.** After a first rejection, the repair batch covers each site that carries the cited defect class and each section that cites, restates, or depends on a repaired section, and the candidate is compared with the retained findings before the re-audit. An audit run now approves when every finding on it is `filed`, so the debt-only rejection exception no longer exists; each `filed` finding is returned in the result and leaves the record unchanged. Before this change, a revision whose findings were all `debt` counted as an approval, and a rejection repaired only the sections its findings named.
- **Merge lifecycle standards disposition a finding by whether the changeset touches or invalidates its text.** A finding on touched or invalidated text is fixed before publication or merge together with its same-class instances and the dependencies the repair changes, a finding on any other text is returned `filed` and recorded in the governing node's `ISSUES.md`, and an Auditor verdict on such other text never blocks the merge. Before this change, `merging-standards` fixed every valid in-scope finding and tracked only a separate larger concern or a verdict on a subject outside the diff, so a finding on unchanged text inside the diff's files held the merge.

## 0.104.6

### Fixed

- **`/apply` no longer stalls between writing tests and implementing them.** Step 6 is now a deterministic check, not an audit gate: it runs validation and the evidence Step 5 wrote, and requires every other test and eval to pass and each new or changed one to fail only because the implementation it verifies is absent. A new test that passes before implementation, or fails for another cause, goes back to Step 5 for repair. Step 8a, after implementation, is the flow's only evidence audit, and it covers cross-node evidence once per governed node and evidence type. Before this change, Step 6 dispatched the test- and eval-evidence auditors before implementation. The flow allows a dispatch only once deterministic verification passes, and tests written ahead of their implementation cannot pass, so that dispatch could never proceed.

## 0.104.5

### Changed

- **`/author-change` launches its `change-auditor` at most twice on one Change candidate.** After the second rejection the skill ends with the record unpublished and reports the outstanding defect class; it never launches a third audit on that candidate. The re-audit before publication counts toward the two, and a re-read that changes the candidate after the second dispatch withholds publication and reports the intervening edit. Before this change, the skill stopped only after three consecutive completed non-approvals.
- **`/author-change` publishes a revision whose audit run is rejected with debt findings only.** A sealed rejected run with no `blocking` finding and every finding at severity `debt` is accepted for publication, subject to the coverage and retained-input checks, and it counts toward neither the two audit dispatches nor the rejections that end the gate. Every other rejection is still a rejection. Before this change, the skill accepted only an `approved` run with no finding.
- **`/audit-change` judges a revision of a published record only on what the revision changes.** When the request carries `issue`, the runner's new `read-published` operation reads the Change's published body from the store. A non-empty body makes the candidate a revision: the audit judges its front matter, every `##` section whose text differs from the published section under the same heading, and unchanged text those changes make false, and records each of their findings as `blocking`. A finding on any other section is recorded as `debt`, and a revision whose findings are all `debt` finishes `rejected` with no `blocking` finding, because SPX seals `approved` only for a run with no finding. A record with no published body, or a request with no `issue`, is judged whole, and any finding still rejects it. `/author-change` puts the stored Change's canonical `<owner>/<repo>#<N>` reference after the candidate path in the `change-auditor` task message for a revision, and the `change-auditor` sets the request's `issue` from it, so the revision path runs for every stored Change. Before this change, every audit judged the whole record and any finding rejected it.
- **`/execute-change` launches each agentic gate at most twice per Change and releases the Change after the second counted rejection.** A rejection counts when a blocking or debt finding sits on a line the changeset changed or is caused by its edit, and a complete `BLOCKED` diagnostic from an audit gate counts as a rejection with no finding to read; the count covers every session, `/merge`'s reviewers and auditors among them, restarts after a published revision of the Change's body, and a third launch of a gate is refused with the count. The Handoff's `Hazards` line names the gate and run token of every counted rejection, so the next Executor continues the count. The Executor launches every Verifier itself; a `change-skill-author` or `change-subagent-author` round's task message tells it to launch no audit or review. The Fixer entry and step 5.5 now state one repair block: the verbatim `/merge` finding for a `/merge` rejection, otherwise every rejected verdict and failed command on the head the previous round produced. Deterministic commands stay outside the cap and still release the Change when they fail again after a Fixer round. Before this change, the skill released only on a repeated defect class, with no count on new ones, and kept verdict run tokens out of the Change.
- **The `change-skill-author` round can no longer launch a subagent.** Its definition now withholds the `Agent` tool alongside the operator-question tool, as `change-author` does. The round therefore cannot launch an audit or review in its own session; the Executor launches every Verifier after the round returns. Before this change, the round could launch `instructions:skill-auditor` itself, and those runs appeared only in the round's session.
- **The `change-subagent-author` round can no longer launch a subagent.** Its definition now withholds the `Agent` tool alongside the operator-question tool, as `change-author` does. The round therefore cannot launch an audit or review in its own session; the Executor launches every Verifier after the round returns. Before this change, the round could launch `instructions:subagent-auditor` itself, and those runs appeared only in the round's session.
- **`/apply` launches each audit or review gate at most twice and stops the flow after the second counted rejection.** A gate is one Verifier definition judging one subject, and the cap now covers the Step 9 whole-changeset review as well as the Step 4, 6, 8 and 8a audits. A rejection counts when a blocking or debt finding sits on a line the changeset changed or is caused by its edit, and a complete `BLOCKED` diagnostic from an audit gate counts as a rejection with no finding to read. A finding already filed in `ISSUES.md`, a stale finding, a finding on untouched text and a launch that seals no run count for nothing. At the stop, the skill reports the gate, both verdicts and the outstanding findings, and it never launches that gate a third time. Deterministic checks stay outside the cap. Before this change, Steps 4 and 6 looped until approval, the audit gates stopped after three consecutive non-approvals, and repeated Step 9 findings had no stop.
- **The merge policy in `merging-standards` runs each agentic gate at most twice per changeset and stops the lifecycle after the second counted rejection.** Each evidence-Auditor predicate is a gate, and the local review and the CI review are two separate gates. A rejection counts when a valid `BLOCKING` or `DEBT` finding, or a rejected, failing or unknown Auditor result, sits on a line the changeset changed or is caused by its edit, and a complete `BLOCKED` diagnostic from an Auditor counts as a rejection with no finding to read. A finding already filed in `ISSUES.md`, a stale finding, a finding on untouched text and a launch that returns no usable result count for nothing. At the stop, the lifecycle reports the gate, both results and the outstanding defect class, and it never launches that gate a third time. Deterministic verification stays outside the cap. Before this change, the local-review, verdict-handling and loop-semantics rules repeated a review or audit until it came back clean, and repeated valid findings never stopped the lifecycle.
- **`/open-pr` runs each evidence Auditor and the local review at most twice before the opening push.** Every re-run after a repair counts toward that gate's cap, as the merge policy in `merging-standards` defines it. A gate's second counted rejection stops the flow with no push and no pull request, and reports the gate, both results with their run tokens and the outstanding defect class. Deterministic verification still re-runs after each repair outside the cap. Before this change, the opening flow re-ran an Auditor until its predicate was clean and looped the review and verification until one tree passed every predicate.
- **`/manage-pr` runs each evidence Auditor and the local review at most twice before a follow-up push.** Every re-run after a repair counts toward that gate's cap, as the merge policy in `merging-standards` defines it. A gate's second counted rejection stops the management pass with no push, and reports the gate, both results with their run tokens and the outstanding defect class. Deterministic verification still re-runs after each repair outside the cap. Before this change, Step 6 ran the local review to convergence and looped every predicate until one tree passed them all.
- **`/merge` runs each evidence Auditor and the local review at most twice before a direct-push.** Every re-run after a repair counts toward that gate's cap, as the merge policy in `merging-standards` defines it. A gate's second counted rejection stops the transport before the push, and reports the gate, both results with their run tokens and the outstanding defect class. Deterministic verification still re-runs after each repair outside the cap. Before this change, the transport re-ran an Auditor until its predicate was clean and iterated the local review to convergence.

## 0.104.4

### Fixed

- **The 0.104.3 entry names the profile change without model identifiers.** It described commit `aabc117050212aa46ed8b46c29cbbd35c1f71713` with literal model names, which the marketplace's validation forbids in authored plugin content. The entry now describes the same change through the profiles. The released behavior is unchanged.

## 0.104.3

### Changed

- **Every spec-tree subagent except `change-executor` runs on a new Claude configuration of the Standard profile.** In Claude Code, the Standard profile now resolves to the model the Executor profile uses, at medium effort. Before, it resolved to the Strong profile's model at medium effort. The evidence and record auditors, `changes-reviewer`, the change-round subagents, and `instruction-block-updater` select Standard. `change-executor` keeps the Executor profile. Codex configurations are unchanged.

## 0.104.2

### Changed

- **`/execute-change` hands a skill-surface Fixer its repair block as repair input.** The Fixer rule no longer names `instructions:create-skill` as declaring no repair-block intake; it names `instructions:create-subagent` alone. A `change-skill-author` Fixer's repair block, the verbatim rejected verdicts and failed commands of the earlier round, is now read by `instructions:create-skill` as its repair input.

## 0.104.1

### Fixed

- **`/sync-base` reports base-sync preservation for a branch whose diff holds bytes that are not valid UTF-8.** The synchronizer reads the diff that feeds `git patch-id --stable` as raw bytes. A clean rebase of such a branch now returns `rebased` with a readiness-preservation proof. Before this fix, the synchronizer stopped with a decoding error and printed no JSON result.
- **`/sync-base` reports a missing `scope-changeset` script as a `git_failure` result.** When the sibling `scope-changeset` skill's `changeset_scope.py` is absent from the installed plugin or fails to load, the synchronizer prints a `git_failure` JSON result whose `detail` names the expected path and exits 1. Before this fix, it exited 1 with a Python traceback and no JSON result.

### Changed

- **`/sync-base` creates recovery checkpoints only through `/commit-changes`.** The skill composes `spec-tree:commit-changes` by exact name, and every `git switch` it runs during dirty-tree recovery is named in its command policy. Its tool grant no longer includes `git branch`, so a `git branch` command the skill runs, `git branch -D` among them, now asks for approval. Its tool grant no longer includes `git switch -c`, so every `git switch` the skill runs during dirty-tree recovery asks for approval, and so does every `git checkout --ours` or `git checkout --theirs` during conflict reconciliation; a prefix grant for those commands would also admit the forms the command policy forbids, `git switch` with a force, discard, or merge option and a blanket `git checkout --ours .` or `git checkout --theirs .`. The grant keeps `git rebase --abort` and now grants `git rebase --continue` only in that exact form, since neither command takes an argument; the skill still runs `git rebase --abort` only on the decision of whoever decides the conflict route. The command policy lists the granted commands apart from the ones that ask for approval.
- **`/sync-base` commits an unrelated coordination note on a branch cut from the base.** The skill first commits objective paths on the objective branch. It then moves the uncommitted note onto `work/<note-slug>` cut from `origin/<base>`, commits it there, and switches back to the objective branch or detached head before it re-runs the synchronizer. The result names the note branch and its full head identity as a separate changeset not yet on the default branch.
- **`/sync-base` reads lane mapping from `spx/local/merging.md`.** Review reuse and the narrowest verification lane after a sync or a resolved conflict read the project's merge overlay. When that overlay is absent, the skill falls back to the full gate.

## 0.104.0

### Changed

- **The implementation audit selects its concern skills from the artifact registry.** `/audit-implementation` reads, for each changed path, the artifacts and audit skills that a registry shipped beside the new `select-artifacts` skill selects. It dispatches the selected concern skills, records the paths of every other selected audit skill as accounting units naming that skill, and records a selected concern skill that is not installed as a `missing-skill` unit. It no longer discovers languages from the installed `code-{lang}` skills.

## 0.103.3

### Changed

- **The router's dangerous-command guard section splits a blocked compound command once.** A block on a command holding one operation with every string written literally still terminates that command family. A block on a command holding a process substitution, a pipe between two operations other than a payload pipe, a background `&`, a subshell, or a list that mixes `&&` and `||` terminates its command family too, because parts run one at a time cannot carry a stream, concurrency, shell state, or a status through a skipped part. A compound command is two or more operations separated by `;` or a newline or joined by `&&` alone or by `||` alone, or one operation whose words the shell expands (a variable, a command substitution, a glob, or a tilde, brace or arithmetic expansion), or a heredoc with an unquoted delimiter whose body expands; a heredoc feeding one command and a pipe whose first stage only supplies its stdin payload each count as one operation, and a payload pipe with an expanding word resolves its values first and runs once with literal words, never split, its family ending when the guard blocks that literal pipe. A block on a compound command directs Claude to resolve each value first, then run its parts again one at a time, in their original order — `;` and a newline separate lists that each run regardless of the one before, and within a list parts joined by `&&` alone run while the part before them succeeded and parts joined by `||` alone run until one succeeds — with every string written literally, and never to print or write a secret value into a command; a part the guard blocks on its own terminates that part's family. Reformulating, stripping the flagged clause, or substituting an equivalent command stays forbidden. Run `/update-instruction-block` to render the section into the root instruction files.
- **`/update-instruction-block` orders a recency tie before its other repairs and names its files without the harness word.** A reported recency tie resolves first through the `--reconcile --from` rerun after the recency writes are committed, and the one-edit-batch step covers only the Edit repairs that follow; the never-rerun rule names that rerun as its one exception. A mutual delegation asks nothing and goes straight to its refusal resolution. The stale conditions are stated once, and the frontmatter description names the product's two root instruction files without the harness word.

## 0.103.2

### Changed

- **The router tells a session to move a file it needs gone to the user's trash.** The instruction block's No File Removal section keeps forbidding every command that deletes a file and now directs a file a task needs gone, outside the exempted removals, to the trash command the host supplies, such as `trash` on macOS, where the operator can restore it. A host with no trash command leaves the file in place and the session reports it to the operator, an instruction from the operator or the repository to keep a file or to report it without removing it takes precedence, and scratch files stay in place. The template advances to 0.41.0, so `/update-instruction-block` re-renders a consumer's router block once its recorded version is behind and the section reaches the root instruction files.

## 0.103.1

### Requires

- **`/diagnose` declares `@outcomeeng/spx` 0.8.0 as the floor.** The manifest's `spx_floor` moves from 0.7.2 to 0.8.0, the release whose `spx validation markdown` enforces the 4.0 link shapes; a consumer on an older `spx` CLI updates it to the floor the manifest declares.

## 0.103.0

### Added

- **`/migrate-3-to-4` converts a 3.x tree's decision citations and forbidden link forms to tree-absolute links.** The skill runs one standalone script over the product root: a decision path written as a code span, a decision link of the citing node, and every `../`, leading-slash, out-of-node and descendant-node link to a file in `spx/` become a Markdown link with a tree-absolute href, and fenced code blocks stay untouched. It prints the rewritten files and every citation it cannot convert, and leaves those unchanged for the operator: a bare path in prose, a decision path a code span holds beside other text, a broken target, a link to a file outside `spx/`, and an assertion evidence link that leaves its node. Exit status 0 means nothing remains unconvertible, 3 means the report lists leftover citations, and 1 means an error stopped the run, with the files already rewritten listed. A second run must rewrite nothing.

## 0.102.0

### Breaking
